title: My first version failed, so I started over. Under Management, two months into the rebuild
author: Don_InterestingSys
selftext:
I'm a solo developer using AI.  Under Management is a 3D isometric game about defending a house dug into a hill. The Guild raid it. You set traps, and they learn to take them apart. You hide an archer behind a wall, they adjust.  Lock the doors and they bring a ram, study how you held the door, and come round the other side next time. The ground changes under everyone.

This is my second attempt. I started in early August. Seven weeks later the first version was stuck, Claude and I could still fix issues but for everything we added we had to fix 5 other things. 

In late September when Opus 5.5 came out I threw it out and started again using the first attempt as a detail for the redesign and build.  Within 3 days we were well past the seven week version one and haven't slowed down since. Everything in the video is filmed in the game's own engine, two months into the rebuild.



What I used:

\- \*\*Claude Code\*\* for the code and the in-game writing

\- \*\*Three.js, TypeScript and React\*\*, with Electron for the Steam build

\- \*\*Nano Banana Pro\*\* for character concepts, then \*\*Meshy\*\* to turn them into 3D models

\- \*\*Freesound\*\* CC0 recordings for the geese, the hound and the rest



The lesson I learned: If you fail, turn the first build into the design for the retry and get back at it as soon as a new model comes out.



I'm hoping to have a Steam page early 2027. For now there's a free demo you can run in your browser: the address is at the end of the video.

Play testers very welcome.  if you try it out please post a comment in the game and point out what you would do differently

comments.author: Don_InterestingSys
comments.body: I'm just starting to capture some videos for the game from the game footage.  It's not my strong suit so any ideas about how to put together a good trailer would be welcome as well.  this one is my first that I've posted so hopefully I get better at it
